audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Aurora level 1 and level 6, while the prose says Poppy grounds her escape from the moment W is up and that 'at 6 she still owns the all-in'. Level 3 was given to Poppy although whys[2] calls it 'your one even window'.
audit.why: Three rows contradicted the explanation printed beside them. The packet chart [Poppy, Skill, Skill, Poppy x4] matches every whys[] line and matches a 42.55% win rate over 47 games; the shipped chart implied Aurora wins the opener against a melee with an 8s 430-range Hammer Shock.
audit.corrected: Chart rebuilt to the packet chart in both layers, ratings dropped to 3/10 on the rows she owns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Steadfast Presence was written as an on-demand switch that deletes Aurora's escape anywhere on the map ('she can ground your Across the Veil leap on demand', 'delete your only escape on demand').
audit.why: Riot's text: activating it stops enemy dashes around her, and a dash that is stopped is slowed and grounded. The ability's range is 400. It does not reach across the lane, and it has to be active. That distinction is the whole matchup: leaping at range is safe, leaping into her is not, and the punish window is the 20s at rank 1 while it is down — which is still shorter than Across the Veil's 22s, so she can hold it more often than you can use the leap.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the 400-unit radius, the stop-then-ground order, and the 20s-versus-22s comparison that decides who wins the cooldown war.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes was the generic 'Steadfast Presence online, level 6, first item / Aurora levels 2-3 (full pattern)'.
audit.why: Aurora has one real window in this lane — level 3 with both spells while Heroic Charge (14s at rank 1) is down — and her level-6 and item spikes do not convert against a tank. Poppy's spikes are W at 2 and her first armour item.
audit.corrected: Spike row rewritten to say exactly that, including that Aurora has very little after Riftmaker.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2], mid, late and wants.you[2] leaned on 'Between Worlds untargetability' and 'walk a wall out'.
audit.why: Riot's text gives the ultimate damage, a slow and a crossable area. Against Poppy the honest version is still good advice — the rift is an escape from the wall-stun — but it works because you cross the zone freely and she is slowed in it, not because you become untargetable.
audit.corrected: Untargetability and wall-walking removed; the escape framing kept on the real mechanic.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late were written in the first person — 'I farm at max Q range', 'I do NOT all-in', 'my W on cooldown' — where every other matchup on the champion addresses the reader as 'you'.
audit.why: It is the only voice break I found in the slice and it reads like a different author mid-page.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten in second person at the same length.

edits.before: Respect this from minute one — the second Poppy has W (Steadfast Presence) she can ground my Across the Veil leap, the only escape I own, so I never jump toward her. I farm at max Q range and chip with the recall second-hit, but I do not step into Heroic Charge (E) range with my W on cooldown, because a wall-pin stun followed by Hammer Shock and autos is a free kill. My one micro-window is around level 3 when her E is down: Q-curse, recall it for the second hit, poke with The Weirding (E) and hop straight back before she can answer.
edits.after: Respect this from minute one — the second Poppy has Steadfast Presence (20s at rank 1) she can stop your Across the Veil leap inside 400 units of her and ground you, so you never jump toward her. Farm at max Q range and chip with the recast second hit, but do not step into Heroic Charge range with your leap on cooldown, because a wall-pin stun into Hammer Shock and autos is a free kill. Your one micro-window is around level 3 while her E is down: curse, recast it for the second hit, poke with The Weirding and hop straight back before she can answer.

edits.before: My passive spirit-heal sustain means little here — she soaks the poke behind her buckler shield and her armor only grows, so the trade math that beats squishy bruisers does not apply to a tank. At 6 I do NOT all-in: Between Worlds can't burst through her health and armor, so I treat R as the escape that finally beats her wall-pin — go untargetable or walk a wall out when she commits Heroic Charge. The whole mid-game is denying her the wall-stun engage and farming, not winning trades.
edits.after: Your passive spirit-heal sustain means little here — she soaks the poke behind the buckler shield and her armour only grows, so the trade maths that beats squishy bruisers does not apply to a tank. edits.before: This stays bad. Once she has an armor item she walks through my full Q-recall-E rotation, and she only needs one Heroic Charge into a wall with my W grounded to kill me, while her Keeper's Verdict (R) knockback makes her a problem in every fight I don't dictate. I look for sidelane farm and pick-offs on her squishier teammates with my poke rather than the 1v1, and I lean on R untargetability purely to survive her engage. Get the lead from elsewhere on the map — this lane is damage control, not a kill lane.

notes: _missing-interactions claims Between Worlds cancels Keeper's Verdict because that ultimate is a channel. Riot's Between Worlds text has no interrupt, stun or knockup in it — the kit's hardCC flag on it looks like a tooltip-parse misfire — so I did not write the interaction. The Aurora-vs-Pantheon mirror audit reached the same conclusion about the same flag, so the two pages agree. Poppy's Hammer Shock also carries a 'grounding' derived flag that Riot's description does not support (it describes damage and a slowing zone); I ignored it. First-person voice in early/mid/late was unique to this matchup in my slice — worth a grep for ' I ' and ' my ' across champ-data/content.
